cards.explanation: The answer is mute idols, friends. Paul says they were "…influenced and led astray to mute idols." Mute means the idols never said a word back. I know something about talking to silence, because a junk drawer isn't exactly a great conversationalist either.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says that when someone is speaking by the Spirit of God, "Jesus be cursed…" is not what comes out. So the claim has it backwards. Someone speaking by the Spirit doesn't say that about Jesus.

The answer is the Holy Spirit, friends. Paul says no one can say, "Jesus is Lord…" except by the Holy Spirit. So those words come with the Spirit's help. And notice who Paul names in the next few verses: Spirit, Lord, God, all in a row.

The answer is God, friends. Paul says "…the same God works all things in all people." Look at the three lines together: same Spirit, same Lord, same God. The ways of working may change from person to person, but the One behind them doesn't.

The answer is everyone, friends. Paul says the manifestation of the Spirit is given to each one "…for the common good." So a gift isn't a trophy for the shelf. It's given for everyone's good, like a warm batch set out for the whole office.

The answer is True, friends. Paul says the message of wisdom comes "…through the Spirit…" and faith comes "…by the same Spirit…" Gifts of healing come "…by that one Spirit…" Different gifts, one Spirit, and Paul keeps saying so.

The answer is that the Spirit gives as He determines, friends. Paul says the Spirit is the one "…who apportions them to each one as He determines." So nobody is picking from a menu. The giving is up to the Spirit, and I think that takes a lot of pressure off the rest of us.

The answer is Christ, friends. Paul says the body is a unit made of many parts, and then adds, "So it is with Christ." Many parts, one body, and Christ is the picture. Paul is about to show what that means for the people reading his letter.

The answer is True, friends. Paul says "…in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, slave or free…" So Jews or Greeks, slave or free, were all baptized into the one body. Different backgrounds, one body.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says the foot saying it's not a hand "…would not make it any less a part of the body." Saying it doesn't belong doesn't take it out. Belonging isn't up to the foot's mood.

The answer is that a body needs all its different parts, friends. Paul asks, "If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be?" And if it were all ear, "…where would the sense of smell be?" A body made of just one part would be missing a lot.

The answer is God by His own design, friends. Paul says "…God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design." Every one of them. So where you sit in the body is God's doing.
The word is need, friends. Paul says the eye cannot say to the hand, "I do not need you." The head can't say it to the feet either. No part gets to look at another part and say it can do without it.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says "…the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable…" Seeming weaker doesn't make a part optional. Every part is needed, and that includes the ones that look small.

The answer is so there would be no division in the body, friends. Paul says God gave greater honor to the parts that lacked it "…so that there should be no division in the body…" He adds that its members "…should have mutual concern for one another." God built the body so the parts would care about each other.

The word is rejoices, friends. Paul says "if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it." When one part suffers, all of them do, and when one is honored, all of them celebrate. It's like the whole kitchen cheering when one batch comes out perfect.

The answer is that not everyone has every gift, friends. Paul asks, "Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers?" and keeps going through miracles, healing, tongues and interpreting. I think the answer he's after is no, since he's just said God appointed different people for different roles.
The answer is True, friends. Right after the questions, Paul says, "But eagerly desire the greater gifts." Then he adds, "And now I will show you the most excellent way." He's not done teaching yet.
